Most houseplants die from overcare: the roots rot long before the
leaves complain. The rhythm that works is to judge the soil by weight
and feel, water thoroughly until it runs out of the drainage holes,
then wait for the top two centimetres to dry before watering again.

Winter slows every plant, and the summer schedule over-waters them.
Drooping stems signal thirst within a day; root rot signals itself a
week too late.
